Empirical semivariogram

Source: R/krg.R
vgemp.Rd

The classical estimator of Matheron (1963): half the mean squared difference of the values over the pairs of points whose distance falls in each of nbins equal bins of (0, cutoff] (the first bin closed at 0). Bins without pairs are left out. The semivariogram describes how dissimilar values become with distance, the first step of kriging: rates of a crime, a disease or a survey outcome measured at places.

Usage

vgemp(x, y = NULL, v, nbins = 15, cutoff = NULL)

Arguments

x, y

The points: x and y numeric vectors of equal length; or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (or X and Y, as sf::st_coordinates() names them, or lon and lat with lonlat = TRUE) and y NULL; or x an sf or sfc object of POINT geometries, whose coordinate reference system must agree with lonlat. An unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y; other columns are never taken by position. Vectors given separately (x, y, and w or t where a function takes them) are matched by name when every one is named and no name repeats, as elsewhere in the package; otherwise by position. No missing or infinite values.

v

The values: finite numbers, one per point.

nbins

The number of distance bins: one whole number from 1 to 67108864 (2^26).

cutoff

The largest distance used: NULL for a third of the largest distance between two points (the convention of gstat), or one positive number.

Value

A data frame with one row per bin holding pairs: dist (the centre of the bin), gamma (the semivariance) and np (the number of pairs).

References

Matheron, G. (1963). Principles of geostatistics. Economic Geology, 58(8), 1246-1266. doi:10.2113/gsecongeo.58.8.1246

See also

Other geostatistics: bkrig(), crsof(), krigcv(), lfspec(), okrge(), sglmx(), smixm(), spobj(), spsamp(), spxy(), trsurf(), vgfit()

Examples

# simulated values with a trend from west to east
set.seed(1)
p <- cbind(x = runif(60, 0, 10), y = runif(60, 0, 10))
v <- p[, 1] * 0.5 + rnorm(60, 0, 0.3)
vgemp(p, v = v)
#>         dist      gamma np
#> 1  0.3883710 0.03235575 14
#> 2  0.6472850 0.10202814 16
#> 3  0.9061991 0.14740942 25
#> 4  1.1651131 0.17579384 27
#> 5  1.4240271 0.12605216 28
#> 6  1.6829411 0.20833025 43
#> 7  1.9418551 0.27639636 43
#> 8  2.2007691 0.37523216 57
#> 9  2.4596831 0.46234587 48
#> 10 2.7185972 0.54284954 60
#> 11 2.9775112 0.68058945 69
#> 12 3.2364252 0.78158842 69
